audit_findings.title: Customer prepayments may be double-counted in cash and future OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $213.823m net deferred revenue at 2026-06-30, equal to 35.6% of $600.979m cash/STI and $5.27 per diluted share; actual valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash collected before revenue recognition can enter the bridge as cash and later enter OE through recognized revenue; avoiding duplication requires the corresponding deferred-revenue working-capital outflow or an excess-cash adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have received a cumulative total of $264.6 million in fixed monthly cash payments that we have not recognized as revenue.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and subsequent recognition are demonstrated, but double counting is not demonstrated because the supplied record lacks the 2025 OE working-capital reconciliation. The balance is large enough to affect the valuation conclusion if the offset was omitted.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $213.823m June 2026 net deferred-revenue balance and the $50.786m recognized above fixed cash payments during first-half 2026 through the OE calculation; rerun after either retaining the working-capital reversal or excluding the associated prepaid cash from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Committed fleet growth may require unmodeled equity reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.164005bn of June 2026 commitments; stated 15%-25% cash funding implies $324.601m-$541.001m, or $8.01-$13.35 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth requires cash-funded aircraft investment, while debt-financed portions also reduce equity OE through interest; omitting required reinvestment makes forecast growth free.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have firm purchase commitments for 69 E175 aircraft and spare engines totaling $2.3 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments and expected cash contribution are demonstrated. The record does not show whether scenario growth is net of this funding, but the implied equity investment is plainly large relative to the $640m bridge addition and could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map all 67 committed aircraft to placements, replacement versus incremental capacity, delivery payments, financing, interest and incremental OE; rerun each scenario with growth-capex cash contributions and financing costs explicitly included.

audit_findings.title: Terminal value extends beyond the disclosed contract horizon
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $1.908bn-$3.093bn of operating PV, representing 46.3%-50.9% of scenario operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: The terminal value assumes continuing OE after most disclosed capacity-purchase contract removal dates, so renewal rates, repricing and post-contract aircraft utilization directly determine terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: Our business model is dependent on code-share agreements with four major airline partners.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved valuation assumption rather than a demonstrated accounting error. United and Delta terms extend only to 2035, American to 2032 and Alaska to 2038, while the terminal period begins around 2036; nearly half the operating valuation therefore depends on replacement or renewal economics not established in the record.
audit_findings.action: Rerun terminal cases with contract-by-contract expirations, renewal probabilities, alternative utilization, transition costs and repriced margins, including a no-renewal or residual-value-only downside case.

audit_findings.title: Nonoperating investment income may be capitalized and separately added
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 stake-related results net to approximately $0.5m pretax; if fully retained, computed capitalization is about $4.0m-$5.9m, or $0.10-$0.15 per share, versus $4.762bn-$6.717bn scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment and equity-method income left in anchor OE would be capitalized while the related stakes are separately included in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income, net primarily consists of the unrealized and realized gains and losses on our investments in other companies, income or loss related to our equity method investments and gains or losses on the sale of assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The reconciliation should still be corrected if necessary, but the filed 2025 amounts—$0.9m Aero Engines income, $1.3m Contour income and a $1.7m Eve loss—produce only about $0.5m of net pretax income. Capitalizing that amount is under 0.1% of each scenario equity value and cannot reasonably change the conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 OE reconciliation and remove the identified stake-related income and losses; confirm that no additional income attributable to the separately added $39.3m stakes remains.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a utilization-recovery year as normal
audit_findings.magnitude: The $387.3m anchor exceeds 2024 OE by $109.6m, or 39.5%; first-half 2026 net income declined $18.428m, operating income declined $29.989m and airline/SWC segment profit declined $60.828m year over year; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An abnormally high anchor raises every forecast OE year and the terminal value, independent of the selected growth rate.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2024, captain attrition began to ease and, by the end of 2025, we were operating full flight schedules requested by our major airline partners.
audit_findings.explanation: The recovery character of 2025 is demonstrated by 14.7% higher block hours and restoration of full requested schedules, but the record does not establish how much of $387.3m is sustainable. Subsequent profit declines despite higher first-half 2026 block hours reinforce that normalization could be material, though they do not prove the correct anchor.
audit_findings.action: Construct normalized OE from comparable full-utilization periods, adjusting for deferred-revenue recognition, maintenance cycles, labor and training costs, fuel exposure, tax items and temporary productivity; rerun all scenarios using the supported normalized anchor.
